traits.short_shoots.note: Hallé, Oldeman and Tomlinson 1978, pp. 59-60: Acer, Betula, Corylus, Fagus and rosaceous fruit trees such as Pyrus have a well-developed short-shoot system, whose short shoots fill most of the crown and bear most of its leaves (Wilson's red maple).

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 genus aggregate for Corylus (gwddagg_v2.2_genus.csv, read): specific gravity 0.53 (wsg_est, the hierarchical-model genus mean, from 18 records in 10 sources); trunks 0.53, branches 0.51. A species with its own measurements states its own. Basic density is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Lowden's key to the birch family: the hazels are shrubs with two-ranked leaves, so one stands at each node.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Lowden's key to the birch family: the hazels' doubly toothed or cut leaves are two-ranked.

traits.flowering_position.note: The Woody Plant Seed Manual's Corylus chapter (read in full): male and female flowers on separate one-year-old lateral twigs; FEIS's Corylus cornuta review (page read): male catkins beside short shoots and female flowers at the ends of short branches.
